note: The gate side of the Phase 4 close, as ported onto the canonical record at branch p4-close-port. The row side is gates/phase4-closure.json; the two meet at the counts below, which validate_inventory.py recomputes from the ledger's entries. implementation_commit is the tree the 26 closures were re-measured against -- de56592, the branch's base. The port changes that tree in one place: the review removed a null test from phys_fn_001986's candidate that the image does not have, outside every closed row's extent, and the asset differential reads the same digest and counts after it. evidence_commit is the commit that published the re-measured ledger and evidence, so the commit adding this file is its child. Phase 4 passes its gate and closes 26 of the 1,050 code rows it owns; its 2,813 data objects and 87 compiler artifacts stand at `classified` and are accounted for by that state. The second number is the one to read. 722 of Phase 4's 1,137 function rows -- 377,842 of its 475,248 code bytes -- are qhull 2003.1 and OPCODE 1.3 VENDORED from pinned archives, present in the DLL rather than proven in it: 3 close, 32 are `reconstructed` on proofs later drives recorded and defer unfalsified, 601 defer `vendored_not_falsified`, and 86 are `classified` -- three of which, phys_fn_005493, phys_fn_005517 and phys_fn_005523, are real functions with a false artifact proof and are escalated below. Every one of the 26 closures was RE-MEASURED on this branch rather than carried: its recorded mutation re-applied in a `git archive` copy of de56592, rebuilt, and run against the pinned DLL between un-mutated controls reading zero, with the oracle digest unmoved -- eaefc573 for NxPhysicsAssetTests, whose fold grew from 21 probes to 30 after the fork, and b87c3219 for NxPhysicsThirdPartyTests. All 25 of the close's own closures survived; phys_fn_002262 moved from mutation O to N because O now also moves the writer's nine cases; phys_fn_004838 spends 10 of mutation A's 20 rather than all of them, because the port's review found, with the harness's print cap lifted, that the other 10 are read only after ~Container() and come from phys_fn_004846's inlined copy of the guard; and the canonical line's phys_fn_002162 closes on its own six published mutations, all six reproducing. Both Phase 4 gates are oracle differentials and Phase 4 registers no staged-pair target, so `run_differential.ps1 -Phase 4` exits the skip code and `run_phase_gate.ps1` admits it. The port also carried a gate-to-phase binding into the validator, and on the canonical ledgers it caught exactly one closure: phys_fn_002344, a Phase 3 row closed on Phase 5's NxPhysicsObjectLayoutTests, which neither -Phase 3 nor -Phase completed runs while Phase 5 is pending. It is re-deferred on the Phase 3 ledger for Phase 5 to discharge, and Phase 3 closes 61 again. The port's review then added the rule that binding was missing: a discharge counts only once the discharging phase is `pass` in program.json. It caught three more canonical closures -- phys_fn_002410, phys_fn_002404 and phys_fn_002406, Phase 2 rows closed on the same Phase 5 target with discharged_by_phase 5 -- and they are re-deferred on the Phase 2 ledger, so Phase 2 closes 56. The review also made evidence_file mandatory for every ledger from Phase 4 on that closes a row, which bound Phase 6's and Phase 7's six closures to evidence/phase6-joints.md for the first time, and enforced the vendored split this ledger's prose drew. What the phase did not do is stated in the ledger's note rather than summarised away: 108 rows are reconstructed and unfalsified, six of them the penetration map's arithmetic that no accepted fixture can see; 315 NovodeX rows were not reconstructed; the mesh column is not reconstructed, so Phase 3's thirteen mesh deferrals do not discharge; seven more deferrals named only Phase 4 and are carried by the deferrals_left_on_passed_phase_4 escalation; and nothing in this phase was ever driven under 0x0f7f.

escalations.summary: 722 census rows and 377,842 bytes -- a third of the function rows in the image -- are not reconstructions. They are qhull 2003.1 and OPCODE 1.3 vendored from pinned archives and compiled into the libraries NxPhysics.dll links. On this branch they fall four ways. 3 carry a mutation inside their own extent and a measured mismatch count, and close. 32 stand at `reconstructed` on proofs later drives recorded and defer `reconstructed_not_falsified`: no mutation is aimed at them. 601, 341,680 bytes, defer `vendored_not_falsified`, a reason whose whole job is to stop 'present' being read as 'proven'; five of them own a family NxPhysicsThirdPartyTests drives and that agrees exactly, which is not falsification, one carries an inlined copy of a statement another row's mutation edits, and 595 have had nothing aimed at them at all. And 86 are `compiler_artifact` and `classified`. 3 + 32 + 601 + 86 = 722. THREE OF THE 86 ARE REAL FUNCTIONS: phys_fn_005493 (Segment::SquareDistance, driven by two registered families that diverge from the image), phys_fn_005517 and phys_fn_005523 (the OPC_AABBTree.cpp pair). Each carries the classification proof 'no product translation unit reaches these bytes', which is false for each -- the same false negative P4 Task 3 found for the 63 rows it retyped -- so on this branch the census makes a driven, divergent function terminal, and `vendored_driven_divergent`, the reason the close added for that one row, holds nothing. The census is the canonical line's and the port did not retype it. P4 Task 2a's own report put the proven count at 'roughly 20 of the 722'; re-derived per row against the standard every closure meets, it is three.
escalations.reproduction: python docs/reconstruction/novodex-physics/tools/validate_inventory.py docs/reconstruction/novodex-physics/inventory.json prints `closure phase=4 closed=26 deferred=1024`; the 601 are the `vendored_not_falsified` entries of gates/phase4-closure.json and their count is recomputed from the entries. build/Release/NxPhysicsThirdPartyTests.exe <oracle dir> <sha256> reports `thirdparty coverage driven=16 divergent=2 words=193028 layout_checks=47` and `thirdparty candidate mismatches=0 layout_failures=0`, and its two `segment_sqrdist` lines name owner=phys_fn_005493 with mismatches=9356 worst_ulp=67 and mismatches=15538 worst_ulp=8420, verdict=divergent. inventory.json gives phys_fn_005493, phys_fn_005517 and phys_fn_005523 kind `compiler_artifact`, state `classified`; evidence/phase4-third-party-map/opcode_map.csv records phys_fn_005493 as reached from LSSCollider::InitQuery at 0x000d34c0.
escalations.evidence: evidence/phase4-falsification.md sections 2, 3 and 7; gates/phase4-closure.json's `deferred_reasons.vendored_not_falsified` and `vendored_driven_divergent` and its note; evidence/phase4-third-party.md for the image-wide map and the spans; evidence/phase4-third-party-map/*.csv for the per-row correspondence.

escalations.summary: The vendored rows' correctness rests on a list of local modifications that is explicitly not proven closed. OPC_AABBTree.cpp was vendored stock while carrying NovodeX code -- an extend axis at BuildSettings+0x0c, a root-BV capture latch at AABBTreeBuilder+0x38, an inflate margin at +0x14 and 28 added builder bytes -- and it was found by a reviewer reading the disassembly, not by any check this repository runs. verify_vendored_sources.py proves External/*/novodex/ contains only real modifications; no artefact proves it contains all of them.
escalations.reproduction: In a `git archive` copy, delete External/opcode/novodex/OPC_AABBTree.cpp, reconfigure, rebuild and run NxPhysicsThirdPartyTests: on this branch five layout assertions fail (`AABBTree.extend_pulls_min=0 expected=3225419776`, `capture_latch_cleared=1 expected=0`, `captured_root_max_y=14093820 expected=1082130432` -- uninitialised stack, 12260066 at bcf544f -- `inflate_min=0 expected=3204448256`, `inflate_max=1082130432 expected=1083179008`) and it exits 1 while `candidate mismatches` stays 0.
escalations.evidence: evidence/phase4-falsification.md section 3; External/opcode/MODIFICATIONS.md, which states that the list is not proven closed. External/qhull/MODIFICATIONS.md does NOT carry that qualifier, checked on this branch; adding it is open.

escalations.summary: USE_MINMAX is defined nowhere in the pinned OPCODE tree and nowhere in External/CMakeLists.txt, so NxOpcode compiles the centre/extents AABB while the image compiles min/max. It is one target_compile_definitions line and it changes the storage of every box across 34 translation units and the float results that follow. sizeof(AABB) is 24 under both representations, so the registered `layout sizeof_AABB=24` assertion cannot see it.
escalations.reproduction: AABB::Add at 0x000e2d20 reads [this+0], [this+4], [this+8] straight into the min with no subtraction, where a centre/extents build emits mCenter[i] - mExtents[i]; _BuildHierarchy's inflate at 0x000f0f8e subtracts the margin from the first Point and adds it to the second. Adding -DUSE_MINMAX to NxOpcode and re-running NxPhysicsThirdPartyTests is the experiment.
escalations.evidence: External/opcode/MODIFICATIONS.md, the USE_MINMAX paragraph; evidence/phase4-pmap-reconstruction.md section 10.

escalations.summary: A falsification that is real, non-zero and aimed at the right rows cannot be spent, because the closure schema has no detection form for it. NxPhysicsThirdPartyTests is registered as an oracle differential, so a row it closes must report `mismatches=<n>`; its 47 layout assertions report `layout_failures=<n>`. Deleting the OPC_AABBTree.cpp overlay fails five of them, aimed at phys_fn_005517 and phys_fn_005523. On this branch the question is one step worse: both rows carry kind `compiler_artifact` on a false classification proof and stand at `classified`, outside any ledger, so the measurement has no row to be recorded against at all. Widening the schema was declined: Phase 2's close was repaired by inventing a step and the repair reintroduced the defect.
escalations.reproduction: The probe run in opcode_modification_list_not_closed. Then read tools/validate_inventory.py: MISMATCHES binds oracle differentials, STDOUT_DELTA and DIFFERENTIAL_DETECTION bind staged pairs, and a static proof must report `check_failed <name>` and name a target in $NxRegisteredStaticProofTargets, which holds only NxPhysicsInternalTests.
escalations.evidence: evidence/phase4-falsification.md section 3; gates/phase4-closure.json's note; tools/gate_targets.ps1's `layout ...` registrations for NxPhysicsThirdPartyTests.

escalations.summary: gates/phase2.json's third_party_container_rows_moved escalation asked Phase 4 to re-close all four Ice/IceContainer.cpp rows Phase 2 had closed on static proofs. One of the four is: phys_fn_004840, Container::Resize, on a mutation of its `mGrowthFactor <= 0.0f` guard reading 36 mismatches, re-measured on this branch. phys_fn_004836 and phys_fn_004847 have no mutation aimed at them; phys_fn_004846's ownership guard is an INLINED COPY of Container::Empty()'s: of the 20 mismatches that mutation produces, the 10 read after Empty() are phys_fn_004838's and are all it spends, and the 10 read after ~Container() come from this copy, which no mutation names as the function it edits. All three stand at `reconstructed` on this branch and defer `reconstructed_not_falsified`. The escalation is discharged for one row of four and continues here.
escalations.reproduction: The `container` family drives Resize, SetSize, Empty and ~Container at growth factors {2.0, 1.5, 0.5, 0.0, -0.0, -1.0, -2.0} crossed with a borrowed buffer and five sizes, and reports ONE count for all four. Weakening Empty()'s guard from `>= 0.0f` to `> 0.0f` gives `container mismatches=20`; with nxReport's eight-line MISMATCH print cap lifted, the 20 are 10 at offset 24 of each 64-word case tape (the entries flag read after Empty()) and 10 at offset 29 (read after ~Container()), on the ten cases with growth factor 0.0f or -0.0f and nb 1 to 5, and none on SetSize's words. Narrowing Resize()'s from `<= 0.0f` to `< 0.0f` gives 36.
escalations.evidence: evidence/phase4-falsification.md section 2; evidence/phase4-third-party-map/opcode_outside_span_map.csv; gates/phase4-closure.json's notes on phys_fn_004836, phys_fn_004842, phys_fn_004846 and phys_fn_004847.

escalations.summary: P4 Task 3 retyped 63 rows from kind `compiler_artifact` to `code` because the recorded classification proof -- 'no product translation unit reaches these bytes' -- is false for every one of them: 35 are the target of a direct call or jmp from another censused row and 28 have their address written into the OPCODE vtable pool at .rdata:0x0011b5a4-0x0011bcf8. It changed nothing else. On this branch none of the 63 carries `third_party`, 53 stand at `discovered` and 10 at `reconstructed`; of the three NovodeX-added BaseModel and AABBOptimizedTree virtuals among them, phys_fn_005380 and phys_fn_005386 are still `discovered` stubs and phys_fn_005382 is now `reconstructed` on a later drive. The same false proof still stands on 86 Phase 4 artifacts, three of which are real functions (see vendored_rows_are_present_not_proven).
escalations.reproduction: evidence/phase4-artifact-retype.csv carries one line per row with the reaching reference; RetypedArtifactsStayCode in tools/tests/test_gate_targets.py binds all 63 to the census and test_the_published_split_is_the_one_the_csv_records asserts the 35/28 split against the CSV's reached_by column. The split was published as 27/36 -- the right total, the wrong halves and the halves swapped -- until the Task 4 review.

escalations.summary: Not one Phase 4 row was ever measured under 0x0f7f. Every mutation pass, both oracle differentials and all 26 closed rows run under the CRT default 0x027f, while in the image at least 21 OPCODE rows sit inside Scene::simulate's closure and two closed rows, phys_fn_004886 and phys_fn_004894, are inside it as well. Those two are provably indifferent -- 232 Capstone instructions across the sixteen in-span extents, zero x87 mnemonics and zero SSE operands -- but Segment::SquareDistance at 0x000f0560 already disagrees with the image by up to 8,420 ULP under 0x027f alone. NxPhysicsCollisionTests is still the only harness that drives both words; neither Phase 4 target can.
escalations.reproduction: gate_targets.ps1 registers `collision control_words default=027f simulate=0f7f` for NxPhysicsCollisionTests and no equivalent line for either Phase 4 target, because neither installs a control word. evidence/phase4-third-party-sources.md section 4.6 records the 21 OPCODE rows by counting jmp edges beside call edges; evidence/phase4-third-party.md section 4 counts direct calls only and says 8.

escalations.summary: Phase 4 did not reconstruct the mesh column, and thirteen Phase 3 deferrals are waiting on it: phys_fn_001757, 001772, 001777, 001779, 001781, 001783, 001870, 001876, 001893, 001895, 001897, 001925 and 001929, every one `blocked_on_later_phase`, `blocked_on_type: TriangleMesh`, `driving_phases: [4]` and the note "It needs the triangle mesh, its acceleration structure and the vertex and index data behind them". Re-derived on this branch from gates/phase3-closure.json: all thirteen are still there, still `discovered`, and none carries an `implementation`. Phase 4 discharged none of them and closed anyway, so `driving_phases: [4]` now names a finished phase. The canonical line's Phase 5 work does NOT answer this: it transcribed the MeshShape constructor (phys_fn_001379) and two MESH shape slots into Physics/src/ObjectModel.cpp, and it recorded that TriangleMesh+0x74 is a reference count, but no Physics/src/MeshShape.cpp exists and nothing on this branch supplies the internal mesh the thirteen wait on. The canonical line's phys_fn_002162, the mesh writer, is a TriangleMesh row and is not one of the prerequisites. Vendoring OPCODE cleared one of four; the other three are Phase 4's own unreached debt -- InternalTriangleMesh, the OPCODECREATE fill at phys_fn_002083, and the accept arm of the mesh reader. The '153 rows of the mesh component' P4 Task 3 counted is not carried: `component` is not an inventory.json key and the count cannot be re-derived.
escalations.reproduction: Read gates/phase3-closure.json and count `deferred` entries whose `blocked_on_type` is `TriangleMesh`: 13, every one with `driving_phases: [4]`; no Phase 4 closed entry carries `discharged_by_phase`. Three of the thirteen carry a `source` -- phys_fn_001876 Physics/src/ContactMeshMesh.cpp, phys_fn_001895 and phys_fn_001897 Physics/src/ContactPlaneMesh.cpp -- and neither file exists: `source` is the ORACLE's translation unit, and on this branch 312 of the 564 rows carrying a path-shaped `source` name a file the tree does not supply. Ten of the thirteen appear in the tree only in tests/PhysicsCollisionTests.cpp's recovered dispatch-matrix table; three appear nowhere.
escalations.evidence: evidence/phase4-pmap-reconstruction.md section 8; gates/phase3-closure.json's thirteen `blocked_on_type: TriangleMesh` deferrals; evidence/phase5-object-model.md section 3e and 3j for what Phase 5 did reconstruct of the mesh shape.

escalations.summary: Seven deferrals besides the thirteen in mesh_column_blocks_phase3_mesh_deferrals name Phase 4 as their only driving phase, Phase 4 passed without discharging any of them, and until the port's review nothing carried them forward. FIVE are Phase 2 rows waiting on the same prerequisite as the thirteen, the internal mesh Phase 4 did not reconstruct: phys_fn_000242 and phys_fn_000478 (createTriangleMesh, the NpPhysicsSDK entry at vtable slot 8 and its PhysicsSDK implementation), phys_fn_000244 and phys_fn_000470 (releaseTriangleMesh, slot 9, and its implementation) and phys_fn_000246 (the outlined unwind of releaseTriangleMesh). Each is `blocked_on_later_phase`, `blocked_on_type: TriangleMesh`, `driving_phases: [4]` and `discovered`; four name Phase 4 blockers among phys_fn_002060, 002065, 002067, 002085, 002140, 002239 and 002258, of which 002067, 002085, 002239 and 002258 are not reconstructed, and phys_fn_000242's note names the need as InternalTriangleMesh teardown. They go to Phase 5 with the mesh the thirteen wait on. ONE is phys_fn_000965, a Phase 2 `homeless_shared_code` row with `driving_phases: [4]`: the 3-byte `xor eax,eax; ret` at 0x000213e0, reconstructed in Physics/src/ObjectModel.cpp and falsified by nothing. ShapeBase::ShapeBase (phys_fn_001273, a Phase 5 row) installs it as the first of the three Prunable owner adapters at .data 0x10128470 (`mov dword ptr [0x10128470], 0x100213e0` at 0x0002563f), it is slot 5 of the box-hull table Phase 5 transcribed, and phys_fn_005111 (Phase 4) tail-jumps to it at 0x000e1541; it goes to Phase 5, whose gate drives that constructor. The same measurement found eighteen more deferrals whose driving phases have all passed and that no escalation carries -- seven Phase 2 Scene rows naming Phase 3 alone and eleven Phase 2 homeless rows naming Phases 3 and 4 -- and they are not carried here: which phase inherits them is undecided.
